title: Arctic polar vortex forecast to collapse earlier than ever recorded
verification: Smithsonian Magazine (Nov 6, 2026, citing Bloomberg, USA Today, Scientific American, Guardian, Newsweek): forecasts say the vortex could collapse within about a week; vortex winds sit roughly 10-30 miles up; records since 1958; NOAA's Laura Ciasto says only two other SSWs documented in November; previous earliest Nov 28, 1968; 2021 disruption contributed to Great Texas Freeze (200+ deaths, 4.5M homes and businesses without power); record 'super' El Nino; researchers unsure of interaction. Fox Weather (Oct 27, 2026): MIT's Judah Cohen calls it the largest, earliest disruption on record in forecasts; timing, strength and impacts highly uncertain. Worded as forecast, not as an event that has happened.

slides.text: Two record-breaking forces, pulling winter in opposite directions. Even the experts say they don't know who wins.

caption:
Twenty miles above the North Pole, something is about to break, and it is forecast to happen earlier in the year than anything on record.

Every winter a ring of fast winds called the polar vortex circles the Arctic, roughly 10 to 30 miles up, and keeps the coldest air near the pole. When the stratosphere suddenly heats up over a few days, those winds can weaken, reverse or even split in two. Cold air that is normally locked in can then slide south.

Reliable records of these events go back to 1958. NOAA meteorologist Laura Ciasto says only two have ever been documented in November, and the earliest was November 28, 1968. Forecasts now point to one within about a week of November 6, 2026. MIT climatologist Judah Cohen has called it the largest, earliest disruption on record in the forecasts.

Why care? A disruption in 2021 helped feed the Great Texas Freeze, which killed more than 200 people and left 4.5 million homes and businesses without power. This time a record "super" El Niño is pulling the other way, since El Niño usually means a milder winter for much of North America.

Nobody knows how those two will interact. Forecasters stress that timing, strength and impacts are still uncertain, and this is a forecast, not a done deal.

So is a cold winter coming, or a warm one? Honestly, the experts are still arguing.

Source: Smithsonian Magazine, Fox Weather
